name: Fallow-Crown

civilization.name: Threl Dominion
civilization.notes: An atomic-age society clinging to a narrowing band of arable land after axial drift wrecked the seasons; their weather-engine array fails more each year and the orbital ark fleet remains unfinished.

specific_features: Derelict space station in orbit (unfinished ark shipyard)
description: From orbit Fallow-Crown looks bruised: ochre grasslands give way to gray dust bowls, and a single hyperstorm, generations old, squats across the southern hemisphere like a second continent. The axial drift that began two centuries ago has stretched seasons into decades-long extremes, and the Threl Dominion now farms a narrow mid-latitude belt between killing heat and deeper killing cold. Rivers that fed the old grain provinces run in braided graveled beds, their deltas stranded far from any sea.

Inside the arable belt, life is loud and anxious: irrigation flumes roar day and night, and the weather-engines thunder on the horizon, hurling ionized chaff at storm fronts to turn them aside. Refugee arcologies stack forty levels deep, smelling of recycled air, wet concrete, and hydroponic basil grown under sodium lamps. Outside the belt, silence; the dust seas swallow sound and settlement alike.

The Threl saw the drift coming a century out and answered with two great works: the weather-engine array holding the green belt, and an ark fleet meant to carry a million of their people to kinder worlds. The engines work, barely, burning uranium reserves that cannot last; the shipyard ring in low orbit stands half-built, cranes still parked mid-lift from the day funding collapsed. Their archives insist the drift is natural, cyclical, survivable, though younger generations have stopped reading them.

To outsiders, the Dominion offers cheap uranium and cheaper labor, and quietly brokers salvage rights to the half-finished arks. Rival ministries argue over whether to finish the fleet for a chosen few or spend everything hardening the belt for everyone, and the weather-engines fail a little more each monsoon. The hyperstorm has recently changed course for the first time in eighty years, and every forecast agrees it is heading straight for the last farmland on Fallow-Crown.
